message.content:
The exact number of mitochondria varies widely between cell types and even within the same cell type depending on metabolic demand. In general:

| Cell type (mammalian) | Typical range of mitochondria per cell |
|-----------------------|----------------------------------------|
| **Neurons** (high energy demand) | ~1 000–10 000 |
| **Cardiac muscle cells** | ~5 000–20 000 |
| **Skeletal muscle cells** | ~2 000–10 000 |
| **Epithelial cells** | ~200–1 000 |
| **Fibroblasts** | ~200–500 |
| **Red blood cells** (anucleate, no mitochondria) | 0 |

For most “typical” non‑muscle cells, you’ll find on the order of a few hundred to a few thousand mitochondria per cell. The exact number depends on factors such as cell size, energy requirements, and the cell’s stage in the life cycle.
